subject: Swiss transfer playbook: clarifying onshore fallback and subprocessor attestations
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@alpinecardio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Swiss transfer playbook: clarifying onshore fallback and subprocessor attestations

Emma —

Following up from our call this morning. AlpineCardio’s ask was that we confirm a defensible approach for the Swiss processing lane (CH) and provide the artifacts you’ll need to get legal/procurement to sign off. To summarize the architecture we propose:

- Primary processing in EU (Frankfurt) under SCCs + TIA where needed.
- Onshore (CH) cache for low-latency read-only prefix caching (encrypted-at-rest, customer-managed keys) as a conditional fallback when EU latency exceeds threshold. No persistent raw logs stored in CH.
- Subprocessors in CH will be limited to: cloud network provider for caching nodes (managed by Redwood), and a monitoring vendor (read-only telemetry). We will provide CSV of the subprocessors and their roles.

What we need from you to accelerate legal review:
1) Confirmation whether AlpineCardio requires a signed UK Addendum in addition to the SCCs/TIA for Switzerland (your legal had a question about cross-mapping).
2) Any procurement constraints on HSM/KMS residency (can you accept customer-managed KMS in EU with keys replicated to CH HSM for the cache?).
3) A short timeline for your review (legal/procurement).

I’ve attached our TIA checklist (redwood_tia_checklist_v1.xlsx) and a draft subprocessor delegation clause for legal to look at.

If it helps, Laura and Rishi are on this thread and can add the legal/technical artifacts we think will close the loop. My ask is: can AlpineCardio produce the subprocessor export (names + addresses + processing roles) and the expected signing cadence by EOD Friday?

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Trust (EMEA Contracts)
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

---
Attachment: redwood_tia_checklist_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18KB)

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@alpinecardio.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@alpinecardio.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 13:04:12 +0100
Subject: Re: Swiss transfer playbook: clarifying onshore fallback and subprocessor attestations

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear summary and the checklist. A few quick items from AlpineCardio legal/procurement:

- Switzerland is a special case for us: we treat CH similarly to the EU for commercial reasons but require a clear mapping to SCCs/TIA artifacts. We are not asking for a separate "Swiss Addendum" but we need explicit mapping docs that show which safeguards apply to CH nodes.
- Procurement flagged the KMS question: we prefer customer-managed keys, but they want confirmation that keys or HSMs will not be shared with any third parties outside the EU unless previously approved. Can Redwood confirm?
- Legal asked whether Redwood can provide a per-subprocessor attestations pack (SOC2 summary + encryption diagrams + retention commitments). A CSV with subprocessor contact + country + role is the minimum we need to start review.

We can reasonably commit to a 3-week legal/procurement review once we receive the CSV and the redlined delegation clause. Contracts will review the draft and come back with redlines.

I’ll loop in our contracts inbox (above). Expect Alps procurement to confirm timelines internally — will update by Friday.

Best,
Emma Jones
General Counsel (interim)
AlpineCardio
emma.jones@alpinecardio.com

---
Attachment: AlpineCardio_subprocessors_Q4.csv (will send in follow-up)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:30:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Swiss transfer playbook: clarifying onshore fallback and subprocessor attestations

Kimberly / Rishi —

Thanks — I reviewed the checklist briefly and sketched an artifacts list we should provide to prevent multiple follow-ups. I recommend we deliver a single package (zipped) containing:

- Subprocessor register (CSV): name, country, processing role, contact, data access level.
- Data flow diagram (high level): EU control plane -> EU model endpoints -> CH cache nodes (read-only) -> metrics/monitoring flows.
- Redlined subprocessor delegation clause (attached).
- SOC2 summary + last audit date for the cache provider and monitoring vendor.
- Encryption design note: key life cycle, where keys are generated, and HSM/KMS boundaries.
- Retention and logging statement: exact retention for request logs, traces, debug dumps (ideally default 30 days, with options).
- Fallback/incident playbook (short): what happens if CH cache is subpoenaed or technical failure occurs.

Operational asks for Rishi: confirm whether CH cache nodes will store any unencrypted request bodies or full KV payloads (we should avoid this). Also, produce a short statement about whether onshore cache can be turned off by customer config.

I’m attaching a draft of the subprocessor delegation clause (subprocessor_delegation_clause_draft.txt) for Alpine legal to start redlining. Once we have Alpine’s CSV I’ll incorporate any country-specific references.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Data Protection
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

---
Attachment: subprocessor_delegation_clause_draft.txt (plain text, 3KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:09:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Swiss transfer playbook: clarifying onshore fallback and subprocessor attestations

Quick technical clarifications for the package:

- CH cache design: KV cache will only hold encrypted prefix tokens. Payloads remain in EU model runtime; cache nodes only serve cached prefixes to reduce token count. No raw user prompts are written to disk unencrypted.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS in EU. For CH cache we can mirror key material using per-customer wrapped key approach inside an HSM located in CH if required (customer must approve key replication). We do not replicate unwrapped keys off HSM.
- Onshore toggle: caching is configurable per-tenant and can be disabled via the account settings API; we’ll include the API snippet in the package.
- Telemetry: monitoring vendor will only receive aggregated telemetry (no PII) and retention is configurable.

I’ll produce two short artifacts: the cache behavior spec (1 page) and the KMS/HSM diagram (1 page). ETA EOD today.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@alpinecardio.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@alpinecardio.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:22:09 +0100
Subject: Re: Swiss transfer playbook: clarifying onshore fallback and subprocessor attestations

Kimberly / Laura / Rishi —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear artifact list. We will:

- Send the AlpineCardio_subprocessors_Q4.csv by EOD today (contains names, roles, and country).
- Contracts will review your delegation clause and return redlines within 5 business days.
- Procurement confirms customer-managed KMS in EU is acceptable provided that any replication to CH HSMs is explicitly authorized in writing.

Two asks from our side before we begin the 3-week review window:
1) Please provide the short KMS/HSM diagram and the cache behavior spec (Rishi mentioned ETA EOD — that will help).
2) Please supply a DocuSign link (or equivalently a placeholder signing flow) so our procurement team can estimate internal lead times.

If those come through today we’ll aim to start the legal review tomorrow and keep to the 3-week cadence.

Many thanks —
Emma Jones
General Counsel (interim)
AlpineCardio
emma.jones@alpinecardio.com
